processing: A tea plant variety rather than a finished tea, best suited to black tea and especially broken black tea: as usual for the class, the leaf is withered, rolled or cut, oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: An early-sprouting variety, so it comes in early in the spring; no picking standard is documented.
appearance_dry: Not documented; as is typical of black tea, dark leaf, broken in the case of broken grades.
appearance_liquor: Not documented; as is typical of black tea, a clear reddish amber.
appearance_wet: Medium-sized leaves, in line with its medium-leaf classification, turning coppery brown as is usual for black tea.
taste_profile: Black tea from this variety is described as mellow with a high, lifting aroma; no fuller tasting notes are documented.

brewing.notes: General advice for black tea, not specific to this variety.

vintage_note: This variety is not usually sold under its own name; it is grown as a companion plant in Guangxi black tea and Liubao gardens.
description:
Paiqi Zhong is a tea plant variety, known by the formal name Camellia sinensis cv. Paiqizhong. It comes from Paiqi village in Shanglin county, Guangxi, and is grown mainly around Damingshan.

Botanically it is a seed-propagated, small-tree type with medium leaves. It sprouts early, is diploid, and grows tall and upright with moderate branching.

Its leaf suits black tea, especially broken grades, which are described as mellow with a high aroma. It tends to be planted as a companion variety for Guangxi black tea and Liubao, so you are more likely to drink it in a regional tea than on its own.

If a seller names it, ask what the leaf was made into and where it was grown.
history:
The variety takes its name from its recorded origin, Paiqi village in Dafeng township, Shanglin county, Guangxi. It is grown mainly in Shanglin and Binyang around Damingshan, and has been introduced to Guilin, Yulin and Liuzhou.

When and by whom it was first selected is not recorded.
